newsitem.title: HUNGARY: HUNGARY SAYS NO CONCESSIONS TO PROTESTING FARMERS.
newsitem.headline: HUNGARY SAYS NO CONCESSIONS TO PROTESTING FARMERS.

text.p: Hungary's Agriculture Minister on Tuesday ruled out further concessions to hardline farmers' union METESZ which plans to disrupt traffic at six border crossings on Wednesday.

"I don't see that further concessions are justified," Frigyes Nagy told Reuters as members of parliament held an emergency debate on tax regulation amendments to which the government agreed after a series of roadblocks set up by METESZ last month.

METESZ farmers plan to slow down traffic by blocking one lane and will attempt to hinder traffic at frontiers with all neighbouring countries except Croatia by repeatedly crossing the border with their cars.

The grouping is one of the smaller but more radical of Hungary's almost thirty farmers' unions which have so far failed to establish a common stance over land ownership, distribution of subsidies and farming taxation.
Nagy said METESZ's claims represent the interests of roughly one-fifth of Hungary's individual farmers.
"I think they stand for about 15 to 20 percent of Hungary's farmers," he said, although he acknowledged that larger numbers of farmers were worried about the sector's future.
"If we look at the more general question of the agriculture's low profitability, more could be affected," he said.
He also said that the ministry had very little room for manoeuvre within the present budget constraints.
"(Financial) sources available for the agriculture are not enough to achieve an improvement in the near future," Nagy said.

Hungary's agricultural output has dropped some 40 percent since the mid-80s and the Socialist-led government, which came to power in the summer of 1994, first presented a long-term farming policy draft at the beginning of March.
Opposition parties, farmers' unions and experts have criticised the draft for not going beyond generalities and failing to address the present crisis.
During Wednesday's emergency debate, however, all opposition parties signalled their intention to vote for the government amendments on tax relief for individual farmers,
"It is better than than nothing, but only by a small margin," opposition Democratic Forum MP Zoltan Bogardi said.
